summary: Late call (the routine fired at 09:31 ET, written 09:37 after the open). Chip and AI-hardware washout after Intel's weak guide (INTC -26% at the open, PC TAM -12%, 'no positive cash flow this year') and Amazon's miss (-4.5%): SPY opened -1.0% at 761.38, QQQ -2.5%, SMH -5.2%. Yields and the dollar are lower and oil higher, so the macro is not aligned for a put; open-to-close is a coin flip with a slight lean down (p_up 0.46): no SPY trade. Sniper GEV call: HSBC upgraded GE Vernova to Buy ($1,100 target) at 08:02, yet the stock opened -4.6% with the AI-capex complex, so the upgrade is not in the price; median target $1,200, 40% above.

Sniper GEV call: HSBC upgrades GE Vernova to Buy with a $1,100 target (Benzinga 08:02; GLJ kept Sell). GEV reported 10-28 (beat, guide raised, $9B Trench deal, buyback doubled to $20B), fell on the report, took four target cuts on 10-29, and opened -4.6% at 846.91 today with the AI-capex selloff; 854.8 at 09:34, above its open. Webull median target $1,200 (low $940). ANALYST.md: upgrades carry (+0.6% median open-close, 57% up), downgrades do not. Risks: power is sold with AI hardware today (VST -1.6%), the upgrade was already public before the open, and a call fights the tape; catalyst_open only buys while GEV is at or above its open

Considered and not named: LLY (+3.6% open gap to a record on RBC $1,600 / JPM $1,650 target raises, the day after its report: target raises are weak catalysts and the gap is over 1.5%), XOM and CVX (reported this morning: XOM beat, dividend up, $20B 2027 buyback), AAPL (reports 11-02, the next trading day; 'dodges worst of smartphone chip meltdown'), V (+1.4% on target raises and Tencent/stablecoin items; we already carry the V 420C), WMT (+1.6%, Apple Pay support is minor), NVDA (talks to give credit support for the Nscale data-center project, 07:31: a financing headline into a chip selloff, not a call catalyst), INTC (KGI upgrade against three downgrades on a -26% report gap)
